newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Eight Timorese in embassy to leave for Portugal.
newsitem.headline: Eight Timorese in embassy to leave for Portugal.

text.p: Eight East Timorese who entered the French Embassy in Jakarta this week were to leave for Portugal on Thursday as eight newcomers prepared to spend their first night in the mission, a diplomatic source said.
"The eight who entered the embassy on Tuesday will most probably leave the embassy and travel to Portugal on Thursday," the source said.

But the source said the eight men who scaled the compound's high steel fence before dawn on Thursday in another apparent asylum attempt would be unable to leave with the first group because there was insufficient time to process their documents.
Police said the second group of Timmorese men, who entered the compound at about 5.30 a.m. on Thursday, had followed the same route their compatriots had taken two days earlier.
Despite the embassy raising its spiked fence to around three metres (nine feet) high last year, East Timorese have entered the French mission 12 times since November 1995.
The embassy has declined to comment on the latest break-in, but Timorese sources said the men who broke into the compound on Thursday were part of an organised asylum bid.
The eight men due to depart on Thursday include university students. They will travel to Portugal under the auspices of the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC).
Since September 1995, 100 East Timorese have entered foreign embassies in Jakarta and been granted asylum in Portugal.
The United Nations does not recognise Indonesia's 1976 annexation of East Timor and regards Portugal as the administering power in the territory.
The Indonesian government has allowed asylum seekers to leave for Portugal with the help of the ICRC.
